title.narrative: Improving the conservation status of the remaining Macaw populations in Northeastern Paraguay

description.narrative: Illegal wildlife trade is a multi-billion-dollar activity and wild birds (especially parrots and macaws, family Psittacidae) are currently threatened with extinction due to the high numbers of individuals involved in domestic and international wildlife trafficking annually. Of the 25 species of parrots recorded in Paraguay, eight are of conservation concern, including six species of concern at the global level, all of which are threatened by illegal pet trade. In fact, data indicates that in Paraguay there are more macaws in captivity than there are in the wild indicating that viable breeding couples in the wild are risk. This project will reduce poaching and trade of Psittacidae in Paraguay, with a specific focus on the Hyacinth Macaw, Blue-and-Yellow Macaw Green-winged Macaw, Blue-winged Macaw and the Yellow-faced Amazon. Specific objectives include assessing Psittacidae population status and assisting local communities to prevent wildlife trade; creating poach-free areas to promote population recovery; conducting national and local public awareness programs on the impact of poaching and the illegal wildlife trade of parrot/macaws; and support law enforcement agents and existing enforcement measures.
